order: The review runner is inherently the driver for one cross-vendor engine, but the inert tier and the verification manifest are review policy and must bind every review path, including the section 5 fallback, where the Director reviews in session because that engine is unavailable, and any future engine. In the protocol document's section 8.3, reword the tier as policy, so whoever reviews verifies the inertness claim from the diff, the runner enforces it automatically for the engine it drives, and a fallback review applies exactly the same rule by hand; declare the manifest the canonical command set for every verifier. In section 5, make the fallback review inherit the full policy, verifying tier claims from the diff, judging the executor's pasted verification against the manifest, and recording the tier and depth actually run. Document the split between policy and transport in the README and in the runner header.
claims: All three sub-items landed. Section 8.3 rewords the tier as policy for whoever reviews, and declares the manifest the canonical command set for every verifier. Section 5 now carries all three inherited obligations, verifying a declared inert-tier claim from the diff, judging pasted verification against the manifest, and recording the tier and depth actually run. The README and runner header document the split. Grepping manifest across the changed files returns three hits, in section 8.3, in section 5, and in the README.
